senses.definition: (South Africa) A journey by ox wagon.

examples: We're planning a trek up Kilimanjaro.

quotes.text: Early the next morning I set off on the long and hazardous trek through jungles and hills into Assam, and regretfully said "good-bye" to the gallant little Burma Railways, which had functioned to the last and played a big part in evacuating many thousands of refugees and wounded soldiers in the path of the rapidly advancing Japanese.
quotes.reference: 1943 November and December, G. T. Porter, “The Lines Behind the Lines in Burma”, in Railway Magazine, page 327:

quotes.text: Young Indians looking for work opportunities have made up a sizeable portion of undocumented migrants in the US, many after making the dangerous trek through Latin America to reach the US southern border.
quotes.reference: 2025 February 7, Esha Mitra, Aishwarya S Iyer and Ross Adkin, “‘Treated like criminals’: Shackling of Indians aboard 40-hour migrant flight sparks new outrage against Trump”, in CNN:

examples: I would drive to the shops from here; you can walk, but it's quite a trek.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To make a slow or arduous journey.

quotes.text: Before that they had been a good deal on the move, trekking about after the white man, who was one of those rolling stones that keep going round after a soft job.
quotes.reference: 1892, Robert Louis Stevenson, The Beach of Falesá:

senses.definition: (intransitive) To journey on foot, especially to hike through mountainous areas.
(South Africa) To travel by ox wagon.
